paragraphs.text: And he said unto his disciples, It is impossible but that occasions of stumbling should come; but woe unto him, through whom they come!
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Ἀνένδεκτόν ἐστιν τοῦ τὰ σκάνδαλα μὴ ἐλθεῖν, πλὴν οὐαὶ διʼ οὗ ἔρχεται·
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de pros tous mathētas autou· Anendekton estin tou ta skandala mē elthein, plēn ouai diʼ hou erchetai·

paragraphs.text: It were well for him if a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
paragraphs.original: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ εἰ λίθος μυλικὸς περίκειται περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔρριπται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἢ ἵνα σκανδαλίσῃ τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ἕνα.
paragraphs.translit: lysitelei autō ei lithos mylikos perikeitai peri ton trachēlon autou kai erriptai eis tēn thalassan ē hina skandalisē tōn mikrōn toutōn hena.

paragraphs.text: Take heed to yourselves: if thy brother sin, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
paragraphs.original: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς. ἐὰν ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ ἄφες αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: prosechete heautois. ean hamartē ho adelphos sou epitimēson autō, kai ean metanoēsē aphes autō·

paragraphs.text: And if he sin against thee seven times in the day, and seven times turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ καὶ ἑπτάκις ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Μετανοῶ, ἀφήσεις αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean heptakis tēs hēmeras hamartēsē eis se kai heptakis epistrepsē pros se legōn· Metanoō, aphēseis autō.

paragraphs.text: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἶπαν οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ κυρίῳ· Πρόσθες ἡμῖν πίστιν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipan hoi apostoloi tō kyriō· Prosthes hēmin pistin.

paragraphs.text: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye would say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou rooted up, and be thou planted in the sea; and it would obey you.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Εἰ ἔχετε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐλέγετε ἂν τῇ συκαμίνῳ ταύτῃ· Ἐκριζώθητι καὶ φυτεύθητι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· καὶ ὑπήκουσεν ἂν ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho kyrios· Ei echete pistin hōs kokkon sinapeōs, elegete an tē sykaminō tautē· Ekrizōthēti kai phyteuthēti en tē thalassē· kai hypēkousen an hymin.

paragraphs.text: But who is there of you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say unto him, when he is come in from the field, Come straightway and sit down to meat;
paragraphs.original: Τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν δοῦλον ἔχων ἀροτριῶντα ἢ ποιμαίνοντα, ὃς εἰσελθόντι ἐκ τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ· Εὐθέως παρελθὼν ἀνάπεσε,
paragraphs.translit: Tis de ex hymōn doulon echōn arotriōnta ē poimainonta, hos eiselthonti ek tou agrou erei autō· Eutheōs parelthōn anapese,

paragraphs.text: and will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐχὶ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ· Ἑτοίμασον τί δειπνήσω καὶ περιζωσάμενος διακόνει μοι ἕως φάγω καὶ πίω, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα φάγεσαι καὶ πίεσαι σύ;
paragraphs.translit: allʼ ouchi erei autō· Hetoimason ti deipnēsō kai perizōsamenos diakonei moi heōs phagō kai piō, kai meta tauta phagesai kai piesai sy;

paragraphs.text: Doth he thank the servant because he did the things that were commanded?
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἔχει χάριν τῷ δούλῳ ὅτι ἐποίησεν τὰ διαταχθέντα;
paragraphs.translit: mē echei charin tō doulō hoti epoiēsen ta diatachthenta;

paragraphs.text: Even so ye also, when ye shall have done all the things that are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which it was our duty to do.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ποιήσητε πάντα τὰ διαταχθέντα ὑμῖν, λέγετε ὅτι Δοῦλοι ἀχρεῖοί ἐσμεν, ὃ ὠφείλομεν ποιῆσαι πεποιήκαμεν.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis, hotan poiēsēte panta ta diatachthenta hymin, legete hoti Douloi achreioi esmen, ho ōpheilomen poiēsai pepoiēkamen.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, as they were on their way to Jerusalem, that he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ αὐτὸς διήρχετο διὰ μέσον Σαμαρείας καὶ Γαλιλαίας.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en tō poreuesthai eis Ierousalēm kai autos diērcheto dia meson Samareias kai Galilaias.

paragraphs.text: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, who stood afar off:
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσερχομένου αὐτοῦ εἴς τινα κώμην ἀπήντησαν δέκα λεπροὶ ἄνδρες, οἳ ἔστησαν πόρρωθεν,
paragraphs.translit: kai eiserchomenou autou eis tina kōmēn apēntēsan deka leproi andres, hoi estēsan porrōthen,

paragraphs.text: and they lifted up their voices, saying, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦραν φωνὴν λέγοντες· Ἰησοῦ ἐπιστάτα, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: kai autoi ēran phōnēn legontes· Iēsou epistata, eleēson hēmas.

paragraphs.text: And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go and show yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, as they went, they were cleansed.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἐπιδείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκαθαρίσθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn eipen autois· Poreuthentes epideixate heautous tois hiereusin. kai egeneto en tō hypagein autous ekatharisthēsan.

paragraphs.text: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, with a loud voice glorifying God;
paragraphs.original: εἷς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἰδὼν ὅτι ἰάθη, ὑπέστρεψεν μετὰ φωνῆς μεγάλης δοξάζων τὸν θεόν,
paragraphs.translit: heis de ex autōn, idōn hoti iathē, hypestrepsen meta phōnēs megalēs doxazōn ton theon,

paragraphs.text: and he fell upon his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Σαμαρίτης.
paragraphs.translit: kai epesen epi prosōpon para tous podas autou eucharistōn autō· kai autos ēn Samaritēs.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answering said, Were not the ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐχὶ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν; οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ;
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen· Ouchi hoi deka ekatharisthēsan; hoi de ennea pou;

paragraphs.text: Were there none found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger?
paragraphs.original: οὐχ εὑρέθησαν ὑποστρέψαντες δοῦναι δόξαν τῷ θεῷ εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀλλογενὴς οὗτος;
paragraphs.translit: ouch heurethēsan hypostrepsantes dounai doxan tō theō ei mē ho allogenēs houtos;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Arise, and go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō· Anastas poreuou· hē pistis sou sesōken se.

paragraphs.text: And being asked by the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God cometh, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:
paragraphs.original: Ἐπερωτηθεὶς δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν Φαρισαίων πότε ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ παρατηρήσεως,
paragraphs.translit: Eperōtētheis de hypo tōn Pharisaiōn pote erchetai hē basileia tou theou apekrithē autois kai eipen· Ouk erchetai hē basileia tou theou meta paratērēseōs,

paragraphs.text: neither shall they say, Lo, here! or, There! for lo, the kingdom of God is within you.
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ ἐροῦσιν· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ἤ· Ἐκεῖ· ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἐντὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: oude erousin· Idou hōde ē· Ekei· idou gar hē basileia tou theou entos hymōn estin.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it.
paragraphs.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ὅτε ἐπιθυμήσετε μίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἰδεῖν καὶ οὐκ ὄψεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: Eipen de pros tous mathētas· Eleusontai hēmerai hote epithymēsete mian tōn hēmerōn tou hyiou tou anthrōpou idein kai ouk opsesthe.

paragraphs.text: And they shall say to you, Lo, there! Lo, here! go not away, nor follow after [them]:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐροῦσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ἐκεῖ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε· μὴ ἀπέλθητε μηδὲ διώξητε.
paragraphs.translit: kai erousin hymin· Idou ekei· Idou hōde· mē apelthēte mēde diōxēte.

paragraphs.text: for as the lightning, when it lighteneth out of the one part under the heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall the Son of man be in his day.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἀστράπτουσα ἐκ τῆς ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰς τὴν ὑπʼ οὐρανὸν λάμπει, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar hē astrapē astraptousa ek tēs hypo ton ouranon eis tēn hypʼ ouranon lampei, houtōs estai ho hyios tou anthrōpou en tē hēmera autou.

paragraphs.text: But first must he suffer many things and be rejected of this generation.
paragraphs.original: πρῶτον δὲ δεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.
paragraphs.translit: prōton de dei auton polla pathein kai apodokimasthēnai apo tēs geneas tautēs.

paragraphs.text: And as it came to pass in the days of Noah, even so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Νῶε, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
paragraphs.translit: kai kathōs egeneto en tais hēmerais Nōe, houtōs estai kai en tais hēmerais tou hyiou tou anthrōpou·

paragraphs.text: They ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
paragraphs.original: ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἐγάμουν, ἐγαμίζοντο, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας.
paragraphs.translit: ēsthion, epinon, egamoun, egamizonto, achri hēs hēmeras eisēlthen Nōe eis tēn kibōton, kai ēlthen ho kataklysmos kai apōlesen pantas.

paragraphs.text: Likewise even as it came to pass in the days of Lot; they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Λώτ· ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἠγόραζον, ἐπώλουν, ἐφύτευον, ᾠκοδόμουν·
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs kathōs egeneto en tais hēmerais Lōt· ēsthion, epinon, ēgorazon, epōloun, ephyteuon, ōkodomoun·

paragraphs.text: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all:
paragraphs.original: ᾗ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ἐξῆλθεν Λὼτ ἀπὸ Σοδόμων, ἔβρεξεν πῦρ καὶ θεῖον ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας.
paragraphs.translit: hē de hēmera exēlthen Lōt apo Sodomōn, ebrexen pyr kai theion apʼ ouranou kai apōlesen pantas.

paragraphs.text: after the same manner shall it be in the day that the Son of man is revealed.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ ἔσται ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκαλύπτεται.
paragraphs.translit: kata ta auta estai hē hēmera ho hyios tou anthrōpou apokalyptetai.

paragraphs.text: In that day, he that shall be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away: and let him that is in the field likewise not return back.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὃς ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι αὐτά, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἀγρῷ ὁμοίως μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω.
paragraphs.translit: en ekeinē tē hēmera hos estai epi tou dōmatos kai ta skeuē autou en tē oikia, mē katabatō arai auta, kai ho en agrō homoiōs mē epistrepsatō eis ta opisō.

paragraphs.text: Remember Lot`s wife.
paragraphs.original: μνημονεύετε τῆς γυναικὸς Λώτ.
paragraphs.translit: mnēmoneuete tēs gynaikos Lōt.

paragraphs.text: Whosoever shall seek to gain his life shall lose it: but whosoever shall lose [his life] shall preserve it.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἐὰν ζητήσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ περιποιήσασθαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, ὃς δʼ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ ζῳογονήσει αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: hos ean zētēsē tēn psychēn autou peripoiēsasthai apolesei autēn, hos dʼ an apolesē zōogonēsei autēn.

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, In that night there shall be two men on one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἔσονται δύο ἐπὶ κλίνης μιᾶς, ὁ εἷς παραλημφθήσεται καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἀφεθήσεται·
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin, tautē tē nykti esontai dyo epi klinēs mias, ho heis paralēmphthēsetai kai ho heteros aphethēsetai·

paragraphs.text: There shall be two women grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
paragraphs.original: ἔσονται δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, ἡ μία παραλημφθήσεται ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα ἀφεθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: esontai dyo alēthousai epi to auto, hē mia paralēmphthēsetai hē de hetera aphethēsetai.

paragraphs.text: [There shall be two men in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.]
And they answering say unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Where the body [is], thither will the eagles also be gathered together.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ, κύριε; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου τὸ σῶμα, ἐκεῖ καὶ οἱ ἀετοὶ ἐπισυναχθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokrithentes legousin autō· Pou, kyrie; ho de eipen autois· Hopou to sōma, ekei kai hoi aetoi episynachthēsontai.
